requirements.text: The SCE-MI infrastructure provides clock (and reset) generation and shared clock control using handshake signals with the transactor.
A special service loop function is provided by the SCE-MI that can be called from an application to give the SCE-MI infrastructure an opportunity to service its communication channels.

The SCE-MI provides a transport infrastructure between the emulator and host workstation sides of each channel, that interconnects transactor models in the emulator to C (untimed or RTL) models on the workstation.
Each message channel is either an input or an output channel with respect to the hardware side.
The SCE-MI infrastructure performs the task of serving as a transport layer that guarantees delivery of messages back and forth between the message port proxy and message port ends of each channel.
Any transactor can instruct the SCE-MI infrastructure to stop the controlled clock and thus cause controlled time to freeze.
All transactors are told by the SCE-MI infrastructure when the controlled clock is stopped.
All transactors are clocked by a free running uncontrolled clock that is provided by the SCE-MI hardware side infrastructure.
The SCE-MI infrastructure shall provide reliable transport with error detection and notification mechanisms to ensure data integrity during message delivery between the host and the emulator.
Define the failure modes for the transport layer and specify the expected behavior (e.g., blocking, error codes, or exception throwing) when the infrastructure cannot guarantee delivery.
Define specific latency targets for message passing and throughput requirements for the communication channels to allow for objective verification of the 'optimized' claim.

Define specific latency budgets (e.g., 'The SCE-MI infrastructure shall deliver a message from software to hardware in under X microseconds') and throughput targets (e.g., 'The interface shall support a minimum sustained throughput of Y messages per second').
Define the maximum allowable latency for the ServiceLoop function and the recommended polling frequency to ensure deterministic performance.

OPEN: The PRD does not specify access control or authentication mechanisms for the communication channels between the host workstation and the emulator. - The SCE-MI shall implement access control to ensure that only authorized software processes can bind to and communicate with the emulator-side message ports.

OPEN: The specification describes a 'ServiceLoop' function that must be called periodically but does not define the maximum latency or jitter allowed for these calls, nor the consequences of failing to call it within a specific timeframe. - Specify the maximum allowable interval between ServiceLoop calls and the system's behavior if the application fails to service the loop within that interval.

OPEN: The PRD does not specify the maximum number of concurrent message channels or transactors supported by the infrastructure. - Specify the maximum supported number of concurrent message channels and transactors (e.g., 'The infrastructure shall support at least 1000 concurrent message channels').
